evidence.s1_requirements: Every point in steps/1.md is met. `BehaviourTree.snapshot()` returns `{version, root}` built from new plain objects (src/BehaviourTree.ts in step1.patch:1922-1927). `BehaviourTreeSnapshot` and `NodeSnapshot` are exported as types (src/index.ts, step1.patch:2163-2169). `restore()` validates the whole snapshot and then restores it (step1.patch:1934-1947). The snapshot keeps node states, child states, the repeat and retry target and current counts (Repeat.ts and Retry.ts getSnapshot), the lotto `selectedChildIndex` (Lotto.ts), and the wait `totalDuration`/`waitedDuration` (Wait.ts:111-129). Remaining wait time is handled for both time modes: `initialUpdateTime = now - waitedDuration` on restore (Wait.ts:153), and the delta time keeps adding to the restored `waitedDuration`. A finished tree restores as finished, and the next step resets it through the existing root reset. The README has an API entry, a full 'Saving and Restoring a Tree' section and a working fs-based example (README in step1.patch:30-85).
evidence.s1_correctness: Every node that holds state beyond `_state` is covered. A grep of private fields in app/src/nodes finds state only in Action (promise), Wait, Repeat, Retry and Lotto, and each one overrides get/validate/restoreSnapshot. Composite and Decorator recurse into their children (Composite.ts and Decorator.ts in step1.patch:2238-2264, 2339-2365). A lotto resolved by its own guard before it picks a child is handled: `selectedChildIndex` may be null when the lotto is not RUNNING (assertSelectedChildIndex, step1.patch:2111-2129). In clock mode the snapshot records the elapsed time up to the moment it is taken (Wait.ts:117-119). Durations are clamped so that negative or infinite delta times still serialise. Guards are stateless and are evaluated again on each step, so guard aborts replay correctly; tests cover while/until aborts. The step-1 Action change from a boolean to a promise identity (Action.ts:49, 120, 132) fixes an existing race that would otherwise break a restore over a tree with a pending promise. The equivalence harness (SnapshotTestUtilities.ts:74-150) compares node details, call logs and snapshots after every step, from every snapshot point, for all node types.
evidence.s2_validation: Each snapshot records a definition fingerprint, built from a normalised definition with defaults applied, branches inlined (including global subtrees), keys sorted and a cyrb53 hash (BehaviourTreeBuilder.ts createDefinitionFingerprint/normaliseNodeDefinition, step2.patch:617-715). The fingerprint is computed once at construction (BehaviourTree.ts, step2.patch:534-535). A mismatch throws "snapshot does not match the tree's definition: ..." (step2.patch:570-574), before structural validation and before any mutation. Arrays are now rejected (step2.patch:557), and missing or non-string definitions are rejected. Tests cover MDSL↔JSON equivalence in both directions, property order, formatting, subtree order, and about 25 kinds of definition difference checked both ways (spec.ts:1353-1470). The not-a-snapshot table covers null, string, number, array, `{}`, `{foo}` and a function (spec.ts:1540-1572). Two tests check that a rejected restore leaves node details, snapshot and onNodeStateChange calls unchanged (spec.ts:1509-1534). A pending promise is saved as READY (Action.ts:194-196), tests show the function and the entry callback are called again, and the limitation is documented in the README (step2.patch:32).
evidence.s3_fixes: Report 1 is fixed at its cause: `Node.restoreSnapshot` now assigns `this._state` directly instead of calling `setState` (step3.patch:224-228). Regression tests check that no changes are reported on fresh or already-stepped trees and that the next step reports RUNNING→SUCCEEDED transitions from the restored states (spec.ts:1057-1118). The agent's own step-1 test that asserted the old behaviour was replaced, which is correct. For report 2 no code changed. A test was added (spec.ts:100-135), but it only uses sinon fake timers. With the real clock, `Wait.getSnapshot` computes `waitedDuration` from `new Date()` (Wait.ts:117-119), so a snapshot taken shortly after `restore(s)` of a running clock-mode wait can differ from `s` by the elapsed milliseconds. That case of the report is never examined. There are no unrelated changes.
evidence.design: Each node type owns its state through overridden `getSnapshot`/`validateSnapshot`/`restoreSnapshot`, which mirrors the existing `getDetails` pattern. The public surface is two methods plus two exported types. Validation runs before any mutation in a two-phase design. The code follows the repository's JSDoc style and naming. Weaker points: `NodeSnapshot` is one flat bag of optional per-type fields rather than a discriminated union. The internal assert helpers live in the same module as the public types (BehaviourTreeSnapshot.ts). `normaliseNodeDefinition` duplicates the node factory's interpretation of definitions and has to be 'kept in step' by hand (step2.patch:637); hashing a description derived from the built nodes would have avoided that.
evidence.tests: The new test/BehaviourTreeSnapshot.spec.ts (about 1,800 lines) uses mocha, chai and sinon fake timers like the existing tests. A reusable equivalence harness replays from every possible snapshot step, with seeded random cloning and copied agent state, for sequence, selector, parallel, race, all, flip/succeed/fail, repeat and retry (fixed, random and unbounded), lotto (weighted and guard-resolved), callbacks, guards, branches, JSON and waits in both time modes. Further tests cover: no new random calls after restore; a new run after a finished tree; time lost while the process is down; mixed time modes; indefinite waits; promise semantics; definition match and mismatch; invalid input; and an unchanged tree after rejection. A regression test was added to test/nodes/leaf/Action.spec.ts for the promise identity fix. No existing baseline test was removed, skipped or weakened.
evidence.docs: The README adds a feature bullet, `snapshot()`/`restore(snapshot)` API entries, a 'Saving and Restoring a Tree' section with a correct example (the `State` and `BehaviourTree` imports exist), a list of what is saved, the wait timing semantics, the definition check, and the pending-promise limitation next to the API (step2.patch:32). It was updated again for the onNodeStateChange behaviour (step3.patch:10, 19, 28). Version History follows the table convention: 4.4.0 with a continuation row for the promise fix, the 4.4.0 note amended in step 2 because that release was not yet out, and 4.4.1 for the bug fix. package.json and package-lock.json were bumped to match.
evidence.process: There are 17 focused commits with conventional prefixes and descriptive messages (commits.txt): separate feat commits per state area, separate docs commits, separate dist rebuild commits, and the existing promise-race fix in its own commit (240be05) before the feature that depends on it. No dependencies were added, and nothing beyond what the steps asked for, apart from the justified promise fix that is noted in Version History. Test-first order cannot be fully verified from the patches.

unmet_requirements: Step 3 report 2: 'a snapshot taken right after restore(s), before any step, should equal s' is only guaranteed with a frozen clock; with the real clock, a running clock-mode wait's snapshot includes milliseconds elapsed since restore (Wait.ts:117-119), and the regression test only uses fake timers
strengths: Every stateful node type owns its snapshot logic, and validation is split from restoring, so a rejected restore cannot leave the tree partly changed. All node types and the edge cases the steps name (lotto ended by its guard, random counts and durations, both wait time modes, finished trees) are handled correctly.

An excellent equivalence harness (SnapshotTestUtilities.assertRestoredTreeMatchesOriginalFromEveryStep) checks node states, agent call order and snapshots after every step, from every snapshot point, for every node type. Tables of definition differences and invalid inputs test the step-2 validation in depth.

The definition fingerprint normalises MDSL and JSON and inlines branches and global subtrees, so equivalent definitions match and any real difference is rejected with the requested message. The README documents the API, the limits and the version history clearly and correctly.
issues: Step 3 report 2 got only a test and no code review of time dependence: `Wait.getSnapshot` reads `new Date()` for a running clock-mode wait, so snapshots taken with no step in between can still differ under a real clock. The regression test hides this by using fake timers.

`normaliseNodeDefinition` copies the node factory's interpretation of definitions (defaults, branch inlining, count shapes) and has to be kept in sync by hand. Any future factory change can silently break fingerprint equivalence or let a different tree pass the check.

`NodeSnapshot` is a single flat type of optional per-node fields rather than a discriminated union, which weakens the exported type, and the internal assert helpers sit in the same module as the public snapshot types.
review.verdict: This is a careful, well-structured implementation: each node type owns its state, validation is atomic, definitions are fingerprinted with MDSL/JSON equivalence, and an unusually rigorous test suite plus thorough README and version updates back it up. The only notable gap is that report 2 was closed by a fake-timer test, without examining the clock-dependent wait snapshot; I would merge it with a follow-up for that.
